data.body:
**[P2] Ensure every drain covers records pending when it starts**

When another drain has already queued a flush, this branch does not widen `_flush_barrier`; when the flush is in flight, `covered` tracks only exported-record counts. A recordless drain that starts after a newer record is queued can therefore share the older flush and return before that record is exported and flushed, leaving buffered telemetry vulnerable to Lambda freeze. Snapshot the global schedule sequence at drain entry, widen any queued barrier to it, and track in-flight sequence coverage so only a flush covering that snapshot is shared. Add queued- and in-flight-flush ordering tests.
